query: NVIDIA data center revenue growth drivers Blackwell networking
normalized: blackwell center data drivers growth networking nvidia revenue

output.content:
**Latest reported period:** NVIDIA’s Data Center revenue was **$89.0 billion in Q2 FY2027** (quarter ended July 26, 2026), rising **18% sequentially and 117% year over year**, making it the company’s principal growth engine. [[1]]

**Blackwell is the core compute driver.** NVIDIA said hyperscale revenue reached **$49 billion**, up **13% quarter over quarter**, driven by sustained Blackwell demand and incremental GPU capacity coming online. [[2]] The underlying demand is a broad AI-infrastructure buildout across hyperscalers, AI labs, AI-native companies, enterprises, and sovereign customers—not solely a small set of cloud buyers. [[2]]

**The product transition raises NVIDIA’s dollar content per AI factory.** Management estimates that its revenue opportunity increased from about **$18 billion per gigawatt for Hopper** to **$25 billion for Grace Blackwell**, because the platform extends beyond the GPU to CPUs, systems, and networking. [[2]] This is important because Data Center growth depends not just on unit volumes, but also on greater system-level content per deployed gigawatt. [[2]]

**Networking is both a direct revenue contributor and an enabler of Blackwell-scale deployments.** NVIDIA’s networking business posted another record quarter and grew **18% sequentially** in Q2 FY2027, while Spectrum-X Ethernet revenue grew **2.6x year over year**. [[2]] In the prior quarter, NVIDIA reported Data Center networking revenue of **$14.8 billion**, up **35% sequentially and 199% year over year**, illustrating the unusually rapid expansion in network attach alongside AI compute. [[3]]

**Technically, the networking opportunity spans multiple layers.** NVIDIA’s platform combines **NVLink** for scale-up connectivity within large AI systems with **InfiniBand or Ethernet** for scale-out networking between systems, allowing it to capture more of the AI-factory bill of materials rather than selling accelerators alone. [[2]] Spectrum-X specifically expands NVIDIA’s Ethernet opportunity, while the company’s full-stack co-design across GPUs, CPUs, NVLink, scale-out networking, systems, software, and algorithms is intended to improve workload performance and increase platform adoption. [[2]]

**Customer-capex and supply are the near-term swing factors.** NVIDIA characterized its forward outlook as supply constrained, citing a cloud-industry backlog exceeding **$2 trillion** and expectations for top-five hyperscaler capex of nearly **$800 billion in 2026** and **$1.3 trillion in 2027**. [[2]] NVIDIA guided total company revenue to **$108 billion, plus or minus 2%, for Q3 FY2027**, while explicitly assuming no Data Center compute revenue from China, which indicates that its outlook is being driven by demand elsewhere. [[1]]

**Bottom line:** Blackwell drives the compute ramp, networking increases content per deployment and supports cluster scaling, and broad AI-factory investment creates the demand backdrop; the principal constraints are the pace of customer capacity deployment and NVIDIA’s ability to supply increasingly complex integrated systems. [[2]]
